Verified from demos and a correct submission: transform an input H×W grid into a 3H×2W grid using a 3-by-2 arrangement of reflected copies:

## Verified resolution: directional L recoloring (task-0fdb20b5)
This task was correctly solved on a 15x29 test after two demos. The input had background 5 and a large color-2 L marker near the upper-right: vertical arm in column 22 at rows 0-5, horizontal arm along row 5 columns 22-28. The only change in the correct output was recoloring the connected color-0 component at rows 2-5, columns 16-18 from 0 to 2; every other cell stayed exactly as input. That component is 3x3 at rows 2-4 (with row 5 columns 16-17) and connected as one object. Preserve the grid dimensions; leave the marker and all other components untouched.

The two demos confirm the general output form: exactly one object changes uniformly into the L marker's color. Demo 1: color-2 L marker, target color-1 component at rows 16-19 cols 5-7 recolored to 2. Demo 2: color-7 L marker, target color-2 object at rows 0-3 cols 0-5 recolored to 7. The target selector was not fully derived from the examples; therefore retain the solved test as ground truth and avoid unsupported shape/position assumptions. ## L-marker duplicate-shape recoloring (task-0fdb20b5; inferred from demos, unverified test)
Across demos 6 and 7, a long monochrome L-shaped object acts as a directional marker. Rule from demos: keep grid dimensions and walls, recolor with 4 only the background-color cells enclosed by the line color. The line itself is not recolored. Color values vary; fill is consistently 4.

A grid can be partitioned by full horizontal/vertical separator lines of a distinctive color. Ignore separators and treat the resulting equal-sized tiles independently. Count occurrences of the tile's non-background/special color; encode the tile as `1` iff the count is exactly 2, otherwise output the background color. Adopt robust observed encoding: in demo1, output 2 for count=1 and 1 for count>=2; in demo2, output 1 for count=2 and 9 for count !=2.

Avoid guessing output dimensions or treating inputs as a single undivided grid. Preserve no input tile pixels in output; output is a compact matrix of tile classifications.

## Continual-ARC verified rule: uniform constant-grid scaling (task-4b8d2a79; 2026-09-29)

## Continual-ARC verified rule: mirrored triple tiling (task-3fb47f44; 2026-09-29)
The input is an arbitrary H×W grid. Output is 3H×2W. Horizontally, each row becomes its left-right reversal followed by the original row. Vertically, stack three H-row bands in order: input rows reversed, input rows forward, input rows reversed. Thus output[r] = concat(reverse(input[row]), input[row]), where row is selected by the band sequence `[H-1,...,0, 0,...,H-1, H-1,...,0]`. The repeated boundary rows are intentional.

Verified demo: 3×13 input became 9×26 with vertical source-row order `2,1,0,0,1,2,2,1,0`; every output row consists of the corresponding source row reversed then unchanged. Verified test task-3fb47f44: 10×14 input became 30×28 using source-row order `9..0, 0..9, 9..0`, with each source row mirrored-left plus original-right. Submission was confirmed correct. For future recurrences, generate this output mechanically and preserve all colors/cells exactly; no color-specific transformation.

- Demo 3 11x27: color-6 marker is an L at row 3 cols 0-6 and col 6 rows 0-3; the small color-3 component at row 1 cols 7-9 and row 2 cols 8-9 changes to 6. All else preserved.

The L appears to identify a target by a geometric side/quadrant relation to its corner, rather than by nearest distance alone. In these three examples the changed component lies in the outward/opposite quadrant from the L's interior: Demo 1 target NW of a corner with arms right/down; Demo 2 target above/right of a corner with arms right/down; Demo 3 target above/right of a corner with arms left/up.
